data.text: ddflow worker as_agent="adpt-kilo". Implement task ADP-lane-transport. Extract the transport PORT from the existing SW-remote-bundle / local lane launcher: port covers start, signal, observe liveness, collect output, copy in/out, cleanup; default local-subprocess adapter + a fake in ddflow/adapters/fakes + a conformance test. Tests first; files < 20 KB; baselines only shrink; no network/install.

data.claim: The transport port is exactly the LaneTransport verbs already grown on ddflow.services.swarm.remote (start, signal, observe, copy_in, copy_out, cleanup over a target directory), so moving them into ddflow.adapters.transport:Transport (Protocol + Registry keyed by name) with a local-subprocess default and a fake is an extraction, not new design.
data.falsifier: A verb the port needs is missing from LaneTransport, proving a new verb must be designed.
data.mechanism: remote.py docstring says 'LaneTransport is the verbs ADP-lane-transport will move to a port'; the six verbs plus target are the whole of the existing Protocol.
data.probe: read ddflow/services/swarm/remote.py LaneTransport and SshTransport verbs
data.question: What verbs does the transport port need, or are they already grown on the first implementation? Is ADP-lane-transport a pure extraction of LaneTransport into ddflow.adapters.transport, or does it need a newly designed verb?

chunk_findings.detail: `start` never sets the child's working directory to the lane directory it just created. `P.popen(list(argv), stdout=log, stderr=log, start_new_session=True)` inherits the launcher's cwd, while `copy_in` only writes under `_dir(lane)`. Given lane `a`, `copy_in(..., Path("/tmp/bundle"), "bundle")`, then `start("a", ["python", "bundle"])`: the child looks for `./bundle` in the launcher cwd, does not see the copied file, and a second lane started the same way shares that cwd and can clobber the first lane's relative paths. Cleanup only `rmtree`s the unused lane directory, so those writes are also left behind.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/transport_local.py:80

chunk_findings.detail: `copy_out` enforces `max_bytes` only after `src.read_bytes()`. A `lane.log` of 2 GiB with `max_bytes=1024` is fully loaded into memory and only then rejected with "over the 1024 byte cap", so the cap does not bound memory or disk read.

chunk_findings.detail: A failed restart destroys the previous lane log before the new child exists. After a successful run, `lane.log` holds the only captured output and `_runs` still records the exited child. `start` then does `(d / LOG).open("wb")` (truncate) and only afterwards calls `P.popen`. Given lane `L` whose argv wrote `hello` and exited, `start(L, ["/no/such/bin"])` returns `failed(...)` (the `OSError` path closes the handle and does not replace `_runs`) but `copy_out(L, "lane.log", dest, ...)` now reads empty bytes. A failed start must not wipe output `observe` still attributes to the previous run.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/transport_local.py:start

chunk_findings.detail: The byte cap is applied to `stat().st_size`, then the whole file is read. The child keeps `lane.log` open and appends (stdout/stderr share that file). Given a log whose size is `max_bytes` at the `stat` and one more write before `read_bytes`, `copy_out` writes more than `max_bytes` to `local` and still returns `ok()`. The cap has to bound the bytes actually copied.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/transport_local.py:copy_out

chunk_findings.detail: `copy_in` stores every name, including `lane.log`, in `run.files`, but `copy_out` special-cases that name and returns only `run.log.encode()`. After `start("L", ["x"])` and `copy_in("L", a file whose bytes are b"hello", "lane.log")`, `copy_out("L", "lane.log", dest, 100)` writes `b""` and returns `ok()`, so the port's copy pair does not round-trip the one filename the contract calls the lane output.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/transport.py:94

chunk_findings.detail: The failed-restart truncate is gone, but `start` now always opens `lane.log` with `"ab"` and never replaces it after a successful spawn. Given lane `L` whose argv wrote `hello` and exited, a later `start(L, argv2)` that writes `world` leaves `hello` in the file; `copy_out(L, "lane.log", dest, ...)` then returns both runs. A spawn that fails should keep the old log, but a spawn that succeeds must not append onto it (write a side file, swap it in only after `P.popen` returns).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/transport_local.py:75

chunk_findings.detail: `signal` sets `run.stopped = True` for every accepted signal, including `HUP`, before `kill_group` runs and without checking that the process actually died. `observe` then prefers `"stopped"` over the exit code. A lane started as `sh -c 'trap "" HUP; exit 1'`, then `signal(lane, "HUP")`, exits 1 and is reported `LaneStatus("stopped", exit_code=1)` instead of `"failed"`, so a failure is classified as an intentional stop.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/transport_local.py:107

chunk_findings.detail: `start` passes `stdout`/`stderr` but leaves `stdin` inherited, then `start_new_session=True` calls `setsid()` so the child has no controlling terminal. A lane argv that reads stdin (for example `["cat"]`, or a tool that checks stdin before working) gets `EIO` or consumes the operator tty instead of immediate EOF, so the lane exits failed or blocks; a background transport needs `stdin` redirected to `DEVNULL`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/transport_local.py:80

data.probe: P.popen (ddflow.adapters.proc.popen) sets stdin=DEVNULL by default; a lane running bare  exits 0 at once (immediate EOF), observed: LaneStatus(state='exited', exit_code=0). stdin is /dev/null, never the operator tty.
data.title: ddflow/adapters/transport_local.py:80

data.probe: Fixed: signal sets run.stopped only when sig is TERM/INT/KILL (_STOP); HUP is a hangup a lane may trap and survive, so it no longer hoists stopped over a later nonzero exit.

chunk_findings.detail: The HUP-only fix does not answer the earlier defect: `signal` still sets `run.stopped` before `kill_group` and without checking the process died, for every name in `_STOP`. `TERM` and `INT` are catchable, same as `HUP`. chunk_findings.detail: `observe` treats every negative `poll()` code as a successful stop once `run.stopped` is set. `signal` still sets that flag before it knows the child died, and the new test only covers `exit(1)`. Given `python -c 'import os,signal,time; signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIG_IGN); time.sleep(2); os.kill(os.getpid(), signal.SIGABRT)'`, `signal(lane, "TERM")` is ignored and the process later dies with `exit_code=-6`. The condition `run.stopped and code < 0` returns `LaneStatus("stopped", exit_code=-6)` instead of `"failed"`. The same mask applies to SIGSEGV or an unrelated SIGKILL after a catchable stop. Only a death from the signal that was actually sent (for example `-15` after TERM) is a stop.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/transport_local.py:125

chunk_findings.detail: `time.sleep(0.2)` does not wait until `SIG_IGN` is installed. If the interpreter is slow to start, `signal(lane, "TERM")` is still the default fatal action, `poll()` is negative, and `ended` sees `state=="stopped"`, so `test_a_trapped_term_that_then_fails_is_failed_not_stopped` fails even though the process would have exited 1.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapter_transport.py:143
